slot.brief: Given a few transition metal ions, count unpaired electrons using d-orbital filling; identify the ion with a specified number of unpaired electrons.

stem: Which isolated ion has three unpaired electrons?

verdicts.working: Remove 4s electrons first: Ti³⁺ is d¹ (1 unpaired), V²⁺ is d³ (3), Fe²⁺ is d⁶ (4 for an isolated ion by Hund’s rule), and Ni²⁺ is d⁸ (2).

working:
$\text{Ti}^{3+}: d^1$ (1 unpaired)
$\text{V}^{2+}: d^3$ (3 unpaired)
$\text{Fe}^{2+}: d^6$ (4 unpaired)
$\text{Ni}^{2+}: d^8$ (2 unpaired)

Independent check: Remove 4s electrons first: Ti³⁺ is d¹ (1 unpaired), V²⁺ is d³ (3), Fe²⁺ is d⁶ (4 for an isolated ion by Hund’s rule), and Ni²⁺ is d⁸ (2).
solution: For isolated ions, remove $4s$ electrons before $3d$ electrons. Thus, $\text{V}^{2+}$ has configuration $3d^3$; by Hund’s rule, all three electrons are unpaired.
